tdg.title: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Certification (TDG)
paragraphs: Our self-directed online TDG certification course was developed by subject matter experts and is designed to provide the enrollee with all the practical skills, knowledge and judgement to adhere to regulatory requirements applicable to nuclear medicine services.

Synergy QMP TDG certification is intended for nuclear medicine technology staff, shippers, couriers and receivers of Class 7 dangerous goods. Included in the course are links to relevant regulatory agencies and resources.

Upon successful completion of the final exam, TDG certification is granted for 3 years (non-transferable). Successful candidates will receive a TDG wallet card, a Certificate of Completion and will earn 1.0 Category A credits from CAMRT / ACTRM. Educational credits are recognized by the CAMRT's provincial organizations and the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT).

objectives.subtitle: In accordance with the requirements of the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act and Regulations.

items.title: Transport
items.body: Become familiar with the regulations for transporting radioactive materials by ground.

items.title: Classification
items.body: Understand the classification standards for dangerous goods in Canada.

items.title: Packaging
items.body: Choose the proper packaging for the transportation of Class 7 packages.

items.title: Marking
items.body: Assign safety marks to radioactive packages and prepare proper paperwork.

items.title: Shipping
items.body: Apply the standard procedures for shipping, handling and receiving radioactive packages.

items.title: Emergency
items.body: React appropriately in case of emergency or possible contamination.
